figures.name: 01_capacity_comparison
figures.title: Throughput and latency under matching loads
figures.caption: Both environments met the project targets through 400 concurrent scripted users. At 500, successful throughput grew modestly while quality targets failed. Red crosses mark any failed test target, including HTTP errors; they do not always indicate a latency failure. On-prem 400/500 are run-level medians. The partial AWS 500 attempt is excluded, and AWS 600/800 were not tested.

figures.name: 02_quality_targets
figures.title: Which target failed at each load
figures.caption: Pass/fail outcomes across tested concurrency levels. Local failures at 500 and 600 were driven by HTTP errors; local 800 and AWS 500 exceeded the latency target. AWS 600/800 were not attempted. Local 400/500 include two trials; the completed AWS 500 repeat is shown, with the earlier abort documented separately.

figures.name: 03_aws_monitoring_timeline
figures.title: AWS load, CPU and healthy targets over time
figures.caption: AWS load bursts occurred while the healthy API target count remained one and no scale-out activity was recorded. The exported five-minute Average CPU stayed below the 50% scaling target. Short bursts can be smoothed by aggregation, so this is not proof that instantaneous CPU never exceeded the target. Gray bands show actual test intervals; the final band is the separately authorized 500-user repeat.

figures.name: 04_monthly_cost_composition
figures.title: What makes up the monthly cost
figures.caption: Cost composition separates hardware allocation and electricity from optional operating allowances. The expanded local budget is S$127.33/month and AWS plus the same operator allowance is S$132.80/month. The minimal local figure is S$52.58; it excludes those extra responsibilities. All power/operating amounts are assumptions, AWS FX/tax are illustrative, and the profiles are not equivalent-service quotations.

figures.name: 05_cash_cost_over_time
figures.title: Upfront and recurring cash cost over three years
figures.caption: Cumulative modeled cash costs include local acquisition costs at month zero and monthly operations thereafter. Depreciation is not added to cash cost a second time. Solid lines show the smaller scope; dashed lines include additional operations. The endpoints depend on the selected scope and assumptions and do not establish equal reliability, capacity or an unconditional saving.

figures.name: 06_paying_sellers
figures.title: Paying sellers required to cover modeled costs
figures.caption: At the proposed S$10 launch price, the gross AWS service budget requires ten paying sellers, or fourteen including the same S$40 operator allowance. S$15 and S$20 are price sensitivities. Counts exclude fees and other business expenses; planned paid features and stated demand do not establish actual subscription revenue.

figures.name: 07_lighthouse_results
figures.title: Browser performance across three Lighthouse runs
figures.caption: The three mobile-emulated Lighthouse scores were 95, 94 and 94, with median 94 against the project target of at least 90. Paint timings were consistent across runs. TBT was 0 ms and CLS 0.115 in all three. These user-supplied lab results are separate from k6 concurrency measurements and actual-user usability findings.

figures.name: 08_endpoint_tail_latency
figures.title: Which endpoints had the longest response-time tail
figures.caption: In the completed AWS 500-user repeat, endpoint median durations were approximately 15–18 ms, while search p95 reached 1,172 ms, detail 546 ms and facets 495 ms. The slow tail caused the overall latency-target failure despite zero observed HTTP errors. Client-side endpoint timings do not isolate the underlying component responsible.

figures.name: 09_aws_budget_drivers
figures.title: Which AWS services dominate the modeled budget
figures.caption: Database, load balancer and public IPv4 costs together represent approximately 77% of the gross US$65.49 monthly model. The small prototype is therefore dominated by baseline infrastructure rather than notification/request volume. This is a launch-planning estimate before allowances, credits and tax, including planned services; it is not the observed daily bill.
